Deleted articles and comments are removed from the database, with no soft-delete flag.
Password reset links stay valid for 30 minutes.
The fancyhash package is not used for password hashing because of its licence.
bcrypt keeps the default passlib work factor.
The article list defaults to 20 items per page.
Favoriting an article sends no notification to its author.
Queries are hand-written SQL files, not generated by an ORM.
Tokens travel only in the Authorization header and never in cookies.
The code talks to PostgreSQL through raw SQL files loaded by aiosql on the asyncpg driver, wrapped in repository classes.
The Authorization header must hold a prefix and a token separated by one space, and the prefix must equal the configured jwt_token_prefix.
Favoriting inserts a (user_id, article_id) row into a favorites join table and ignores duplicates.
Settings are pydantic BaseSettings classes chosen by the APP_ENV value and cached with lru_cache.
Tags are stored as unique text rows in a tags table and linked to articles through an articles_to_tags join table.
Only the comment's author, matched by username, may delete a comment.
HTTP errors are returned as JSON of the form {"errors": [detail]} with the exception status code.
Article lists page with limit and offset query parameters, defaulting to limit 20 and offset 0.
Passwords are hashed with bcrypt through passlib CryptContext, with a per-user bcrypt salt prepended to the password.
Article slugs are generated from the title with the slugify library.
Tests live in a top-level tests folder split into test_api, test_db, test_schemas and test_services, with shared fixtures in conftest.py.
Access tokens are HS256 JWTs that expire one week after issue.
Access tokens are signed with the HS256 algorithm using one shared secret key.
Every access token carries the fixed subject claim access.
Each user gets a random salt created with bcrypt.gensalt.
Request validation failures return HTTP 422 with an errors list of the validator's error objects.
Registering with a username or email that is already taken is answered with HTTP 400.
Only an article's author, matched by username, may modify the article.
Cross-origin calls are allowed from the origins in allowed_hosts, which default to every origin.
The database pool is fixed at 10 connections through min_connection_count and max_connection_count.
Creating a tag that already exists is ignored by the insert statement.
Creating an article whose generated slug already exists is refused with HTTP 400.
